In the same year he also presided over the Muslim League session at Amritsar. Do not confuse him with his brother Hasan Imam, who presided over the Bombay special session of the Congress in 1918.

questions.question:
[Q.111 · Bihar]
Consider the following statements about Dr. Rajendra Prasad:
1. He started the Hindi weekly 'Desh' in 1920.
2. He presided over the Bombay session of the Indian National Congress in 1934.
3. He presided over the Ramgarh session of the Indian National Congress in 1940.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad founded the Hindi weekly 'Desh' (1920) during the Non-Cooperation Movement and presided over the Bombay session of 1934, the same year he led relief work after the great Bihar–Nepal earthquake (15 January 1934). The Ramgarh session of 1940, held in Bihar (now Jharkhand), was presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, so statement 3 is wrong. Prasad also became Congress President in 1939, after Subhas Bose resigned.

questions.question:
[Q.112 · Ancient & Medieval History]
Match List-I (Member of Shivaji's Ashta Pradhan) with List-II (Function):
List-I
a. Mantri (Waqia-navis)
b. Sumant (Dabir)
c. Senapati (Sar-i-Naubat)
d. Nyayadhish
List-II
1. Commander-in-chief of the army
2. Administration of justice
3. Keeping daily records of the king's activities and court
4. Foreign affairs and relations with other states
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: In Shivaji's council of eight ministers, the Mantri (Waqia-navis) kept the daily records and intelligence of the court; the Sumant (Dabir) handled foreign affairs; the Senapati (Sar-i-Naubat) commanded the army; and the Nyayadhish administered justice. The Peshwa (Mukhya Pradhan) headed the council. The Sachiv (Shuru-navis) handled royal correspondence; do not confuse him with the Mantri.

questions.question:
[Q.113 · Ancient & Medieval History]
Consider the following statements about the Vakatakas:
1. Prabhavatigupta, daughter of the Gupta ruler Chandragupta II, was married to the Vakataka king Rudrasena II and ruled as regent after his death.
2. Several of the later caves at Ajanta, such as Caves 16 and 17, were excavated in the reign of the Vakataka king Harishena.
3. The Vakatakas ruled from Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The marriage alliance with the Vakatakas gave Chandragupta II a friendly power in the Deccan, and Prabhavatigupta governed as regent for her minor sons (her Poona copper plates record this). The Ajanta Cave 16 inscription mentions Varahadeva, a minister of Harishena. The Vakatakas ruled the Deccan from centres such as Nandivardhana and Vatsagulma; Pataliputra was the Gupta capital, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
[Q.114 · Ancient & Medieval History]
According to Megasthenes' 'Indica', the municipal administration of Pataliputra was carried on by:
options: a council of 30 members divided into six boards of five members each
a single nagaraka appointed by the king with eight assistants
an assembly of all householders that met once a year
questions.explanation: Megasthenes, the Seleucid envoy to Chandragupta Maurya's court, describes Pataliputra as a parallelogram on the Ganga–Son confluence, ringed by a wooden wall with 64 gates and 570 towers. He says the city was run by 30 officials in six boards of five, each looking after a subject such as industries, foreigners, registration of births and deaths, trade, sale of manufactured goods and collection of a tax on sales. He also divided Indian society into seven classes. The original 'Indica' is lost; it survives in quotations by Strabo, Arrian and others.

questions.question:
[Q.115 · Ancient & Medieval History]
Consider the following events:
1. Defeat of the Huna ruler Mihirakula by Yashodharman of Malwa
2. Alexander's battle with Porus on the banks of the Jhelum (Hydaspes)
3. Reign of the Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda)
4. Conquest of Malwa by the Huna chief Toramana
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events given above?
questions.explanation: Alexander fought Porus in 326 BCE; Menander, the Indo-Greek king of Sakala whose dialogues with Nagasena are recorded in the 'Milindapanho', ruled in the 2nd century BCE; Toramana conquered Malwa around 500 CE (Eran boar inscription); and his son Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman around 528 CE (Mandsaur inscription). So the order is 2-3-4-1. Option C is tempting but puts the son's defeat before the father's conquest.

questions.question:
[Q.116 · Ancient & Medieval History]
The Venetian traveller Marco Polo praised the rule of a queen who belonged to which dynasty, with its capital at Warangal?
questions.explanation: Rudramadevi (c. 1262–1289) of the Kakatiya dynasty ruled from Warangal (Orugallu). Marco Polo, who landed at Motupalli port in her kingdom, praised her justice. The Yadavas ruled from Devagiri and the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra. Her grandson Prataparudra II was the last Kakatiya ruler; he was defeated by the forces of the Delhi Sultanate in 1323.

questions.question:
[Q.117 · Ancient & Medieval History]
Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Devagiri, which he renamed:
questions.explanation: In 1327 Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital to Devagiri, renamed Daulatabad, to control the Deccan better, but later moved back to Delhi. He also issued token currency of copper/bronze (1329–30), which failed because it was easily forged. Tughlaqabad was built by his father Ghiyasuddin, and Jahanpanah was the walled city he himself built in Delhi.

questions.question:
[Q.118 · Ancient & Medieval History]
Babur's memoirs, the 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' (Baburnama), were originally written in:
questions.explanation: Babur wrote his memoirs in his mother tongue, Chagatai Turkish; they were translated into Persian under Akbar by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan. In them Babur describes his victories at Panipat (1526, over Ibrahim Lodi) and Khanwa (1527, over Rana Sanga). Persian is the tempting answer because it was the court language of the Mughals.

questions.question:
[Q.119 · Ancient & Medieval History]
'Amuktamalyada', a work by the Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya, was composed in which language?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) of the Tuluva dynasty wrote 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu. It tells the story of the Vaishnava saint Andal and also has advice on statecraft. His court had eight great Telugu poets, the 'Ashtadiggajas', including Allasani Peddana. He also wrote 'Jambavati Kalyanam' in Sanskrit.

questions.question:
[Q.120 · Art & Culture]
Match List-I (Folk dance) with List-II (State):
List-I
a. Garba
b. Bihu
c. Lavani
d. Ghoomar
List-II
1. Rajasthan
2. Maharashtra
3. Assam
4. Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Garba is Gujarat's circular dance of Navratri; Bihu is Assam's festival dance of spring (Rongali Bihu); Lavani is Maharashtra's fast-paced folk performance to the dholki; and Ghoomar is Rajasthan's swirling dance of the Bhil community and Rajput women. Garba was inscribed on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in December 2023.

questions.question:
[Q.121 · Art & Culture]
The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his victory over:
questions.explanation: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza, the 54-metre-high gateway of the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri, around 1575 to commemorate his conquest of Gujarat (1572–73). Fatehpur Sikri itself honours Sheikh Salim Chishti. In later Mughal buildings, such as Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb and the Taj Mahal, pietra dura (inlay of semi-precious stones) and the char bagh (four-fold garden) became hallmarks.

questions.question:
[Q.122 · Bihar]
The Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:
questions.explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple Complex was inscribed in 2002, the first UNESCO World Heritage Site in Bihar. The first temple there was built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, and the present temple dates from the 5th–6th centuries; it is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built wholly in brick that still stands from the late Gupta period. The site also has the Vajrasana (Diamond Throne) and a descendant of the Bodhi tree. The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara were inscribed in 2016.

questions.question:
[Q.123 · Bihar]
Patna came to be called 'Azimabad' in the early 18th century after:
options: Azim-us-Shan, grandson of Aurangzeb and governor of Bihar
Azim Khan, a general of Akbar
questions.explanation: Prince Azim-us-Shan, son of Bahadur Shah I and grandson of Aurangzeb, was governor of Bengal and Bihar; around 1704 he renamed Patna 'Azimabad'. Patna is also the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh (1666). The gurdwara built there, Takht Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib, is one of the five Takhts of Sikhism, and its present building was raised largely under Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

questions.question:
[Q.124 · Bihar]
The Sonepur Mela at Harihar Kshetra, one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, traditionally begins on:
questions.explanation: The fair begins on Kartik Purnima (October–November), when pilgrims bathe in the holy rivers and worship at the Harihar Nath temple, which is dedicated to both Vishnu (Hari) and Shiva (Hara). It is linked with the Gaj–Grah legend and was once famous for its elephant trade. It runs for about a month.

questions.question:
[Q.125 · General Mental Ability]
Which set of letters, filled in the blanks in order, completes the following letter series?
a b _ a a _ c a _ b c _
questions.explanation: The series is the group 'abca' repeated: abca | abca | abca. Filling the blanks gives c, b, a, a, so the answer is 'cbaa'. Checking 'cbab' gives abcaabcabbcb, which breaks the pattern.

questions.question:
[Q.126 · General Mental Ability]
Three triangles are drawn with a number at each corner and one number in the centre:
Triangle I: corners 2, 3, 4; centre 81
Triangle II: corners 1, 5, 2; centre 64
Triangle III: corners 3, 6, 1; centre ?
Which number should replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Centre = (sum of the corners)². Triangle I: (2+3+4)² = 9² = 81; Triangle II: (1+5+2)² = 8² = 64; Triangle III: (3+6+1)² = 10² = 100. The product rule does not fit (2×3×4 = 24, not 81).

questions.question:
[Q.127 · General Mental Ability]
A cube is painted red on all its faces and then cut into 64 identical smaller cubes. How many of the smaller cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation: 64 small cubes means 4 along each edge (n = 4). Cubes with exactly two faces painted lie along the edges, excluding the corners: 12 edges × (n − 2) = 12 × 2 = 24. For comparison, 8 corner cubes have three faces painted, 6 × (n−2)² = 24 have one face painted, and (n−2)³ = 8 have none (8 + 24 + 24 + 8 = 64).

questions.question:
[Q.128 · General Mental Ability]
In a certain code, 'P # Q' means P > Q, 'P @ Q' means P < Q, 'P $ Q' means P = Q, 'P % Q' means P ≥ Q and 'P & Q' means P ≤ Q.
Statement: A # B, B $ C, C % D
Conclusions:
I. A # D
II. B % D
Which of the conclusions follow?
questions.explanation: Decoding: A > B, B = C, C ≥ D, i.e. A > B = C ≥ D. Then A > D, so I (A # D) is true, and B ≥ D, so II (B % D) is true. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question:
[Q.129 · General Mental Ability]
Arrange the following in a logical sequence:
1. Harvesting
2. Sowing
3. Ploughing
4. Irrigation
5. Marketing
questions.explanation: A crop cycle runs: the field is ploughed (3), seeds are sown (2), the crop is irrigated (4), harvested (1) and the produce is marketed (5). So the order is 3, 2, 4, 1, 5. Sowing cannot come before ploughing, and irrigation is needed before harvest.

questions.question:
[Q.130 · General Mental Ability]
How many 5s in the following sequence are immediately preceded by 3 and immediately followed by 7?
3 5 7 2 3 5 9 5 7 3 5 7 1 3 5 7 8 5 7 3 5 4 6 3 5 7 5
questions.explanation: The '3 5 7' pattern occurs at positions 1–3, 10–12, 14–16 and 24–26, which is 4 times. The other 5s fail the test: in '3 5 9' and '3 5 4' the 5 is not followed by 7, and in '9 5 7' and '8 5 7' it is not preceded by 3.

questions.question:
[Q.131 · General Mental Ability]
Statement: Several cases of dengue have been reported from a residential colony soon after the monsoon.
Courses of action:
I. The municipal body should take up anti-larval spraying and get stagnant water removed from the colony.
II. All residents of the colony should be shifted to another locality until the season is over.
Which of the courses of action follow(s)?
questions.explanation: A course of action should be practical and solve the problem. Dengue spreads through Aedes mosquitoes that breed in stagnant water, so anti-larval spraying and removing standing water (I) attack the cause directly. Moving the whole colony (II) is impractical and far out of proportion to the problem.

questions.question:
[Q.132 · General Mental Ability]
One morning after sunrise, Ravi and Mohan were standing face to face, talking. Ravi's shadow fell exactly to his right. In which direction was Mohan facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning the Sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. Ravi's shadow is to his right, so his right is west, which means Ravi faces south. Mohan stands facing Ravi, so Mohan faces north.

questions.question:
[Q.133 · Arithmetic/Maths]
A rectangular field measures 60 m by 40 m. A path 5 m wide runs all round it on the outside. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: Outer rectangle = (60 + 2×5) × (40 + 2×5) = 70 × 50 = 3,500 m². Field = 60 × 40 = 2,400 m². Path = 3,500 − 2,400 = 1,100 m². A common slip is to add the width only once on each dimension (65 × 45 − 2,400 = 525 m²). Shortcut: 2w(l + b) + 4w² = 2×5×100 + 100 = 1,100 m².

[Q.135 · Bihar]
Gokul Jalashay, one of the two wetlands of Bihar added to the Ramsar list in September 2025, is:
options: a reservoir on the Son river in Rohtas district
a 'tal' wetland of the Mokama group in Patna district
an oxbow lake on the southern edge of the Ganga in Buxar district
a hill lake on the Kaimur plateau
questions.explanation: Gokul Jalashay (448 ha) in Buxar district is an oxbow lake on the southern side of the Ganga. Its water level rises and falls with the river's floods, and it supports more than 50 bird species and the fishing and farming of nearby villages. Its designation, announced in September 2025 together with Udaipur Jheel, took India's count of Ramsar sites to 93. Bihar's first Ramsar site was Kanwar Jheel (Begusarai).

questions.question:
[Q.136 · Bihar]
The six-lane Aunta–Simaria bridge over the Ganga, inaugurated by the Prime Minister in August 2025, has been built parallel to which older bridge?
questions.explanation: The 1.86 km Aunta–Simaria bridge on NH-31, built for over ₹1,870 crore and inaugurated on 22 August 2025, links Aunta (Mokama, Patna district) with Simaria (Begusarai). It runs parallel to the old two-lane rail-cum-road Rajendra Setu (1959), which is in poor condition. Officials say it cuts the detour for heavy vehicles by up to 100 km. Mahatma Gandhi Setu joins Patna and Hajipur.

questions.question:
[Q.137 · Bihar]
The 'Mukhyamantri Pratigya Yojana', approved by the Bihar Cabinet in July 2025, provides:
options: an unemployment allowance of ₹1,000 per month to graduates for two years
a monthly stipend of ₹4,000–6,000 to youth aged 18–28 doing internships, depending on their qualification
interest-free loans up to ₹10 lakh to youth for starting enterprises
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Approved on 1 July 2025, the scheme pays interns ₹4,000 (Class 12 pass), ₹5,000 (ITI/diploma) or ₹6,000 (graduates/postgraduates) a month for 3 to 12 months, with extra support for placements outside the home district or state. Applications are made on the cmpratigya.bihar.gov.in portal. The ₹1,000 allowance in option A resembles the older Swayam Sahayata Bhatta under the Saat Nischay, a different scheme.

questions.question:
[Q.138 · Bihar]
The Gaya Industrial Smart City at Dobhi, one of the 12 industrial smart cities approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024 under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, is part of which corridor?
questions.explanation: On 28 August 2024 the CCEA approved 12 industrial smart cities in 10 states (about ₹28,602 crore). Gaya (Dobhi), spread over about 1,670 acres, is a node on the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC), which runs alongside the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor. The other AKIC nodes approved at the same time include Rajpura–Patiala (Punjab) and Agra and Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.question:
[Q.139 · Bihar]
Jhandu Kumar of Nalanda (Bihar), who won a bronze medal, India's first medal at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, competes in:
questions.explanation: Jhandu Kumar, from Harnaut in Nalanda district, won bronze in the men's heavyweight para powerlifting event at Glasgow 2026 (23 July – 3 August 2026), India's first medal of the Games. Para events are integrated into the Commonwealth Games programme, and medals in them count in the main tally. Source: Drishti IAS state CA, 28 July 2026.

questions.question:
[Q.140 · Current Affairs (National)]
Consider the following statements about the FIH Men's Junior Hockey World Cup 2025:
1. It was held in Chennai and Madurai.
2. Spain won the title, defeating Germany in the final.
3. India won the bronze medal, defeating Argentina.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Germany won its eighth Junior World Cup title, beating Spain 3–2 in a shoot-out after a 1–1 draw (December 2025); this was Spain's first final, so statement 2 reverses the result. India came back from 0–2 to beat Argentina 4–2 for bronze on 10 December 2025, its first podium finish since 2016 (it was fourth in 2021 and 2023).

questions.question:
[Q.141 · Current Affairs (National)]
Mohanlal, conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for the year 2023, is the second personality from Malayalam cinema to receive it after:
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting announced the award in September 2025, and it was presented at the 71st National Film Awards ceremony on 23 September 2025. Adoor Gopalakrishnan (award for 2004) was the first Malayali recipient. The award, instituted in 1969 with Devika Rani as the first recipient, is India's highest honour in cinema.

questions.question:
[Q.142 · Current Affairs (National)]
At the World Para Athletics Championships 2025, held in New Delhi (September–October 2025) and the first edition hosted by India, India's medal tally was:
questions.explanation: India won a best-ever 22 medals (6 gold, 9 silver, 7 bronze) at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, beating its 17 medals at Kobe 2024. Simran Sharma became India's first world para champion in the 100 m. Brazil topped the table with 15 golds, while China won the most medals in all.

questions.question:
[Q.143 · Current Affairs (National)]
'Rudra', announced by the Chief of the Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi on Kargil Vijay Diwas (26 July 2025), is:
options: a light commando battalion for swift strikes along the borders
an all-arms brigade integrating infantry, mechanised units, armour, artillery, special forces and drones
an indigenous anti-drone system developed by DRDO
questions.explanation: Rudra brigades are integrated all-arms formations meant for the Line of Actual Control in eastern Ladakh and Sikkim; they bring combat, support and drone elements under one commander. In the same speech the Army Chief announced 'Bhairav' light commando battalions, which is option A. Both are part of the Army's restructuring after Operation Sindoor.

The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting of 2025, which adopted the 'Gyeongju Declaration', was held in which country, and which economy chairs APEC in 2026?
questions.explanation: Leaders of APEC's 21 economies met at Gyeongju, Republic of Korea (31 October – 1 November 2025), under the theme 'Building a Sustainable Tomorrow'. They also endorsed an APEC AI Initiative. China chairs APEC in 2026, and Viet Nam will host in 2027. India is not a member of APEC.

Who won the men's and the women's singles titles at Wimbledon 2026, respectively?
questions.explanation: Jannik Sinner kept his title by beating Alexander Zverev 6-7, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4 (12 July 2026). Linda Noskova won her first Grand Slam by beating fellow Czech Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 (11 July 2026). Option B, Sinner and Swiatek, were the 2025 champions.

questions.question:

In Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 (released February 2026), India was ranked:
questions.explanation: India ranked 91st of 182 countries and territories with a score of 39/100, up from 96th (score 38) in the 2024 index. Denmark (89) stayed at the top. India's score is below the global average of 42.

questions.question:
[Q.148 · Current Affairs (International)]
NASA's ESCAPADE mission, launched in November 2025 on Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, is designed to:
options: bring back soil samples from the Martian moon Phobos
study, with twin spacecraft, how the solar wind interacts with the magnetosphere and upper atmosphere of Mars
land a nuclear-powered helicopter in Jezero crater
map subsurface water ice for future crewed landings on the Moon
questions.explanation: ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) uses two small spacecraft built by Rocket Lab to study how the solar wind strips away Mars's atmosphere. It was launched on 13 November 2025 on New Glenn's second flight (NG-2), the flight on which Blue Origin first landed the booster. Sample return from Phobos is the aim of Japan's MMX mission, not ESCAPADE.

questions.question:
[Q.149 · Current Affairs (International)]
Which team won the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026, whose final was played at Lord's in July 2026?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Australia beat hosts England by seven wickets in the final at Lord's on 5 July 2026, reaching 151 with 17 balls to spare, for a record seventh Women's T20 World Cup title. Beth Mooney scored 64. England's only title remains the first edition (2009), which was also decided at Lord's.

questions.question:
[Q.150 · Current Affairs (International)]
Who became the Prime Minister of Hungary in May 2026, after his Tisza party won the parliamentary election of April 2026?
questions.explanation: Tisza won 141 of the 199 seats, a two-thirds majority, in the 12 April 2026 election, ending Viktor Orbán's 16 years in power, and Parliament elected Péter Magyar Prime Minister on 9 May 2026. Tamás Sulyok is the President of Hungary, not its head of government. Katalin Novák was President until 2024.
